evaluationParameters: Capillary or sensor glucose rises above 70 mg/dL after treatment and sweating, tremor, and impaired concentration resolve.
Glucose remains within the individualized target range during and for several hours after subsequent cycling sessions, without recurrent or delayed hypoglycemia.
missingInformation: Timing, type, and dose of insulin relative to cycling
Timing and carbohydrate content of the pre-exercise meal or snack
Whether low sensor readings were confirmed by capillary glucose
Occurrence of delayed or nocturnal hypoglycemia after cycling
Availability of fast-acting carbohydrate and glucagon
priorityActions: Stop cycling and promptly consume 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate.
Collaborate with the diabetes care team to establish an individualized exercise-day carbohydrate and insulin-adjustment plan before further cycling sessions.
reasoning: The repeated temporal association with cycling, adrenergic and neuroglycopenic symptoms, and glucose values below 70 mg/dL strongly support exercise-induced hypoglycemia. Immediate treatment and prevention of recurrence through individualized exercise-day planning are the priorities.

stemEvidence.evidence: Sweating, tremor, and difficulty concentrating occurred during or shortly after cycling.
Continuous glucose monitor readings during symptomatic episodes were 58–64 mg/dL.
Episodes occurred on three cycling days, while noncycling-day fasting and premeal glucose remained 95–140 mg/dL.
The preexisting meal and insulin plan continued without an exercise-day adjustment.
